:::{#thm-matmul-product-of-sums}
#### Product of two sums of matrices

For $m \times k$ matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$
and $k \times n$ matrices $\matr{C}$ and $\matr{D}$,

$$
(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{C} + \matr{D})
= \matr{A}\matr{C} + \matr{A}\matr{D} + \matr{B}\matr{C} + \matr{B}\matr{D}.
$$

Each product keeps its factors in the order they appear on the left,
because matrix multiplication is not commutative.
So $\matr{A}\matr{D}$ and $\matr{B}\matr{C}$ are not collected into $2\matr{A}\matr{D}$.

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} + \matr{B})(\matr{C} + \matr{D})
&= (\matr{A} + \matr{B})\matr{C} + (\matr{A} + \matr{B})\matr{D}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib, from the left)}
\\ &= \matr{A}\matr{C} + \matr{B}\matr{C} + \matr{A}\matr{D} + \matr{B}\matr{D}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib, from the right, twice)}
\\ &= \matr{A}\matr{C} + \matr{A}\matr{D} + \matr{B}\matr{C} + \matr{B}\matr{D}
&& \text{(matrix addition is commutative)}
\ea
$$

:::
